body.statement: Does there exist a total synthesis algorithm which, for every exactly encoded rational \(T\), \(\alpha\), compact \(\mathcal K\), and \(\varepsilon>0\), chooses finite \(K\) and rational \(h\) and returns a finite certificate \(\Gamma\) with \(\operatorname{Verify}(\iota,\Gamma)=1\)? Every accepted output must consist of finitely many rational polyhedral observable and nuisance cells, total endpoint-grid policy tables, and outward-rounded Poisson tail and enclosure data; acceptance must imply a measurable deterministic connected-interval family honest for every \(s\in\mathcal S_T\), every \(\kappa\in\mathcal K\), and every maintained nuisance value, together with \(b_\varepsilon\le\overline D_{\mathrm{det}}(\mathcal K)\le U_\varepsilon\) and \(0\le U_\varepsilon-b_\varepsilon\le\varepsilon\). The lower object must be a finite-support integer program accompanied by a complete exact branch-and-bound proof, not an unresolved linear relaxation. The algorithm must also accept an output for \(\iota_{\mathrm{kill}}=(3,1/20,[1/100,1/100],2,1/100,1/20)\) with the mandated \(K=2\) and \(h=1/100\), a globally share-uniform deterministic primal, and an integer lower certificate within \(1/20\). This finite verifier guarantee strictly strengthens Schafer and Stark (2009), Theorem 6, which gives convergence for finite-prior Monte Carlo risk rather than deterministic termination or continuum honesty, and Andrews, Cheng, and Guggenberger (2020), Section 2, which gives qualitative drifting-subsequence uniformity rather than a finite cover, computable enclosures, or a machine-checkable acceptance predicate.
body.justification: This is the theorem-level open content: a finite accepted proof object must replace both nuisance sampling and qualitative compactness at exact coverage contacts.
body.gap: Schafer and Stark (2009), Theorem 6 and the Conclusion, provide finite-prior Monte Carlo convergence but no terminating continuum-honesty verifier or complete integer lower proof; Andrews, Cheng, and Guggenberger (2020), Section 2, provide qualitative subsequence criteria but no finite polyhedral cover, outward error ledger, or decision predicate.
body.consumer: Auditors can replay exact-rational checks and certify sparse-count confidence policies simultaneously for every observed cohort composition and calibrated intensity in the declared domain.

obligation.what_is_open: A terminating synthesis proof must refine the finite closed cover by profile-validity regions into finitely many rational polyhedral observable cells, including nominal-coverage and target-endpoint contacts, and must construct the mandated early-kill primal and complete integral lower tree.
obligation.obstruction: Fixed-design exponential--polynomial separation terminates only for strict rational comparisons. At a zero-margin contact, interval refinement does not determine on which side a profile remains honest or risk-feasible; the profile-validity boundaries can be curved and are not shown to admit a finite rational-polyhedral refinement with one uniformly valid table per cell. The current core also contains no explicit early-kill policy table or exact branch-and-bound witness from which acceptance could be checked.
obligation.attempted: Count truncation and outward endpoint rounding give a uniform error ledger; finite action-profile enumeration gives exact finite nuisance witnesses at each fixed design; semialgebraic stratification gives finitely many critical components at algebraic fixed designs; and the global task reduces to a finite closed-cover condition. These routes certify strict-margin regions but do not resolve exact contacts or produce the required globally share-uniform early-kill artifacts.
obligation.partial_result:
For fixed \(K\) and \(h\), let \(\mathcal A\) be the finite set of complete endpoint-grid profiles and, for \(a\in\mathcal A\), define
\[
 \mathcal R_a(r)=\left\{(s,\kappa)\in\mathcal S_T\times\mathcal K:
 \inf_{\nu}q_a(s,\kappa,\nu)\ge1-\alpha,
 \quad
 \sup_{\nu}r_a(s,\kappa,\nu)\le r
 \right\}.
\]
Upper semicontinuity of coverage, continuity of risk, and compactness of the nuisance box imply that every \(\mathcal R_a(r)\) is closed.  A pointwise endpoint-grid policy of risk at most \(r\) exists exactly when
\[
 \mathcal S_T\times\mathcal K=\bigcup_{a\in\mathcal A}\mathcal R_a(r),
\]
and choosing the first valid profile gives a Borel selector.  At each fixed algebraic \((s,\kappa)\), strict coverage and risk comparisons reduce to the finitely many exponential--polynomial critical components proved above, while the finite-profile argument supplies an exact finite nuisance witness set for the integer optimum.

For the mandatory early-kill values, the part of the outward budget forced solely by count truncation and endpoint rounding is already strictly below the requested tolerance:
\[
 L\tau_2+2h
 =\frac52\,9\left[1-e^{-3/25}
 \left(1+\frac3{25}+\frac12\left(\frac3{25}\right)^2\right)\right]
 +\frac1{50}
 <0.026<\frac1{20}.
\]
Thus more than \(0.024\) of the tolerance remains for the primal--integer gap and outward enclosures.  What is not proved is that the closed cover above has a finite rational-polyhedral refinement carrying uniformly valid profiles at all zero-margin contacts, nor has a primal table and complete integer branch-and-bound witness for this early-kill instance been constructed.
